problem:
Which of the following matrices are block diagonal?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying Block Diagonal and Block Triangular Matrices
examples.problem:
Which of the following matrices are block diagonal?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041065/assets/a610512000d95e3ed80559431e25501a9d498d342e7c180864720bbeb2ee10d4.png)
examples.worked_solution:
A block diagonal matrix can be partitioned so that it has only square blocks on the main diagonal, and all the other blocks contain only zeros.

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is a block diagonal matrix. Indeed, we can partition it as follows:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041065/assets/f6e977aff21319bb8e0cbb251d36577966f84060e809e3485f9019e85cd3538e.png)

- $B$ is *not* a block diagonal matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041065/assets/597e27b2f470bc60717eb3341d2f3e87f411c0a4c796a58ee3aa83c691971517.png)

- $C$ is *not* a block diagonal matrix since it can't be partitioned in the way described above:

$$
\begin{aligned}C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$A$ only."

feedback.problem:
A partitioned matrix $M$ contains the following blocks: 

- ${M}_{11},$ which is a $2\times 3$ block

- ${M}_{12},$ which is a $2\times 2$ block

- ${M}_{22},$ which is a $1\times 2$ block

What are the dimensions of ${M}_{21}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We have a matrix of the form

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}{M}_{11} & {M}_{12} \\ {M}_{21} & {M}_{22}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2\times 3 & 2\times 2 \\ ?\times ? & 1\times 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, ${M}_{21}$ must be a $1\times 3$ block.
